The overhaul is complete and verified. Here is my report.

## Web-hosting preview template — complete overhaul

Rewrote the beginner-audience shared-hosting preview to the flagship quality bar (studied `GameLandingCombined.tsx`), on the same design system. All changes are confined to own-template files plus read-only imports of the shared `MigrationScreens`, `ReviewBadges`, `icons`, and `Frame`.

**Files changed** (all absolute):
- `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/marketing/webhostingtemplate/WebHostingTemplate.tsx` — full rewrite
- `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/marketing/webhostingtemplate/data.ts` — friendlier copy, new `FAQS` + `priceNum`, removed dead `MIGRATION_STEPS`/`RATING_*`
- `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/marketing/webhostingtemplate/kit.tsx` — removed the plain `StarRow` atom
- `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/(marketing)/preview/web-hosting/page.tsx` — server-renders `ReviewBadges` + JSON-LD, richer metadata

**What was done, against each task:**

1. **Whole-page overhaul.** Asymmetric/editorial sections throughout, beginner-friendly plain-language copy. Added migration proof-points and a new **FAQ section** (native `<details>` accordion, no extra JS). Reuses `eyebrow`/`grad-text`/`btn-deploy`/`tone-panel`/`card`/`rail`/`hero-aura`/`pv-*` — no new globals.

2. **Section 2 (price chart) rebuilt on-brand.** Nxeon bars are now violet→cyan (`brand-500`→`accent-cyan`); the competitor is **amber-only**, used strictly as the "price hike" warning with up-arrow indicators on the rising years — the old garish rose+amber is gone. Added gridlines, a dashed **"Flat forever"** guide line at Nxeon's height, and a `role="img"` aria-label.

3. **Glow-box sharp-cutoff fixed.** New `AuraGlow` helper renders each outer glow as a blurred (`blur-3xl`), rounded, radial-gradient-to-transparent layer as a **sibling behind** the panel (outside its `overflow-hidden` clip) — matching the fixed ModsTemplate pattern. Applied to hero, chart, control-panel and migration visuals. The popular plan card (which has its own `backdrop-blur` stacking context) uses a feathered box-shadow instead, so its glow bleeds cleanly.

4. **Terminal/code imagery reduced.** Deleted the terminal-styled `MigrationFlow` entirely; the hero setup card is now friendly plain-language rows (no mono build-log); replaced the `🔒` emoji with `IconLock`. The page now leans on the browser/site frame and the clean control-panel dashboard. (Minimal mono is kept only for numeric dashboard readouts — a dashboard convention, not a terminal.)

5. **Free-migration section uses `MigrationScreens`.** The animated migration motion graphic replaces the old terminal image, with a feathered glow and three beginner proof-points.

**Shared requirements:** plain stars replaced by the real `ReviewBadges` (rendered in the server page, passed as an RSC slot into the client template; shown in hero + reviews header); emoji replaced with `icons.tsx`; proper metadata + `ProductOffersJsonLd` (offers from `PLANS`) and `FaqJsonLd` (from `FAQS`); `globals.css` untouched.

**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` shows **zero errors in my files**. The only 3 errors in the run are pre-existing and belong to the separately-modified `components/marketing/aihostingtemplate/` (its own `data.ts` exports `RATING_AVG` but the component references it unimported) — unrelated to this work and importing nothing I changed. Did not run `npm run build` or a dev server.
